1: All wisdom is from the Lord
Wisdom was created before all things, and God poured her out on those who love him. The fear of the Lord is the beginning, fullness and crown of wisdom.
Reverence for God is the root of a wise life.
2: "My son, when you come to serve the Lord, prepare yourself for trials." Gold is tested in fire. Has anyone trusted in the Lord and been disappointed?
3: Whoever honours his father atones for sins. Help your father in his old age, even if his mind fails. Be humble.
The fourth commandment spelled out with tenderness.
4: Do not turn from the poor
Do not make the needy wait. Wisdom tests her children at first, then gladdens them. Fight to the death for truth.
Charity, and courage for the truth.
5: Do not say, "His mercy is great; he will forgive." Do not delay turning to the Lord. Be quick to hear and slow to answer.
Presuming on forgiveness is a trap.
6: "A faithful friend is a sturdy shelter; whoever finds one has found a treasure." Test a friend before trusting.
Real friends are rare and beyond price.
7: Do no evil. Do not seek high office. Honour your priest, stretch out your hand to the poor, visit the sick. "In all you do, remember the end of your life."
Remembering death keeps us from sin.
8: Do not quarrel with the powerful or the hot-tempered. Do not despise the old, for we too will grow old.
9: Guard your eyes and heart. Do not abandon an old friend. Do not envy a sinner's success.
10: A wise ruler makes a stable people. "Pride is the beginning of all sin." Why are dust and ashes proud?
11: The bee is small, but her produce is sweet. Do not find fault before you investigate. Call no one happy before his death.
Only the end shows what a life was.
12: Care in doing good; false friends
Never trust an enemy; his malice corrodes like rust.
13: "Whoever touches pitch gets dirty." The rich use the poor and drop them.
14: Blessed is the one who has not sinned with his tongue. A miser's wealth is no use to him. Do good before you die.
Generosity now; you cannot take it with you.
15: Do not say, "God made me sin." He set fire and water before you: stretch out your hand to whichever you choose.
A clear statement of human freedom and responsibility.
16: Do not rejoice in many godless children. Do not say, "I am hidden from the Lord."
No one is lost in the crowd before God.
17: God gave people tongue, eyes, ears and a mind, and made a covenant with them. "How great is the mercy of the Lord to those who turn to him."
18: A human life is a drop in the sea, so God is patient. A kind word is better than a gift. Before falling ill, humble yourself.
19: Whoever despises small things falls little by little. "Have you heard something? Let it die with you." Question a friend before believing a rumour.
20: Some keep silent and are wise. A slip on the pavement is better than a slip of the tongue.
21: "Have you sinned? Do so no more, and pray about your former sins." Flee from sin as from a snake.
Repent, and do not go back.
22: Mourn for a fool more than for the dead. Remain loyal to a friend in his poverty.
"Who will set a guard over my mouth?"
23: "Lord, Father and Ruler of my life," keep me from proud eyes and evil desire. Warnings against swearing and adultery.
Ask God for help with speech and purity.
24: Wisdom came from the mouth of the Most High and made her home in Israel. "I am the mother of fair love." She is the book of the covenant.
The Church applies this chapter to Our Lady.
25: Harmony among brothers, friendship among neighbours, and a wife and husband who live as one are beautiful. The crown of the old is experience.
A good marriage is one of life's best gifts.
26: "Happy the husband of a good wife." Her beauty in a well-kept home is like the sun rising.
A warm portrait of a good spouse.
27: As the kiln tests the potter's vessels, a person is tested by how he talks. Whoever betrays a secret destroys trust.
28: "Forgive your neighbour's wrong, and then your sins will be pardoned when you pray." The blow of the tongue breaks bones.
The same teaching Jesus gives in the Our Father.
29: Lend to your neighbour in need, and repay on time. Store up almsgiving in your treasury.
30: A father who loves his son corrects him. Health is better than any gold. Do not give yourself to sorrow.
Discipline, health and a cheerful heart.
31: Sleeplessness over wealth wastes the flesh. Blessed the rich man found blameless. Wine in moderation is life.
Moderation in money, food and drink.
32: If you are made master of the feast, do not be puffed up. Speak briefly. Do nothing without counsel.
Good manners are part of wisdom.
33: No evil will befall the one who fears the Lord. God made days and people different, like clay in the potter's hand.
Keep control of your own affairs while you live.
34: Dreams are empty hopes. Offering sacrifice from what was stolen from the poor is like killing a son before his father's eyes.
God does not accept worship paid for by injustice.
35: Keeping the law is itself an offering. "The prayer of the humble pierces the clouds."
God hears the poor and the wronged.
36: "Have mercy on us, O God of all." Gather the tribes of Jacob. Then sayings on choosing a wife.
37: Some friends are friends in name only. Seek advice from a godly person, and above all pray to the Most High.
38: "Honour the physician, for the Lord created him." Pray, and also call the doctor. Mourn the dead, then be comforted. Craftsmen keep the world going.
39: The one who studies the law of the Most High will pour out wisdom. "All the works of the Lord are very good."
Study of Scripture is a calling.
40: Much labour is created for everyone, from birth to burial. But the fear of the Lord is like a garden of blessing.
Life is hard; reverence for God is its shelter.
41: "O death, how bitter is the thought of you" to one at peace with his possessions. A good name lasts for ever.
Death is feared most by those most attached.
42: What to be ashamed of and what not. Then praise: God has ordered all things, and nothing is made in vain.
43: A hymn to the splendour of sky, snow, storm and sea. "He is the all."
We can never praise God enough.
44: Let us now praise famous men
The praise of Israel's ancestors begins: Enoch, Noah, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
Holiness is remembered and held up as an example.
45: Moses, beloved of God and men; Aaron and his priesthood; Phinehas.
God chose and equipped leaders for his people.
46: Joshua, Caleb, the judges and the prophet Samuel.
Faithful leaders in war and peace.
47: David praised God with his whole heart. Solomon was wise in youth and stained his honour later.
Even the great are judged honestly.
48: Elijah arose like fire. Elisha was filled with his spirit. Hezekiah and Isaiah.
49: Josiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, the twelve prophets, Zerubbabel, Nehemiah.
The line of the faithful continues to the author's day.
50: A splendid description of the high priest Simon leading the Temple liturgy, like the morning star among clouds.
A picture of Israel's worship at its best.
51: The author thanks God for rescuing him from death and tells how he sought wisdom from his youth. "Come to me, you who are untaught."
The book ends in thanksgiving and an invitation.
